entities.name: The Gathas
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
Seventeen hymns in Old Avestan, attributed to Zarathushtra (Zoroaster) himself, forming the oldest and most sacred portion of the Avesta and among the oldest religious texts in any Indo-European language (c. 1500–1000 BCE). The Gathas are deeply personal, poetic, and philosophically profound — Zoroaster addresses Ahura Mazda (the Wise Lord) directly, describing his prophetic call, his struggles against hostile priests and tribal leaders, and his revelation of the cosmic struggle between Asha (Truth/Righteousness) and Druj (the Lie/Deceit).

Each human must choose which side to support through thought, word, and deed. This binary moral framework became one of the most influential theological innovations in human history.
